trail: Wikiquote’s Wayne Dyer page ↗ groups its book quotations by title, and this line sits in the Pulling Your Own Strings (1978) subsection — a sourced placement, though the page cites no page number for any quotation on it. That is the anchor, and this record does not go beyond it.

The Internet Archive’s catalogue record ↗ confirms the edition behind that citation: Pulling Your Own Strings, T. Y. Crowell Co., New York, 1978. Confirming that the edition exists is not the same as confirming the sentence is in it, and the scan is lending-restricted, which is where we stopped.

Wikipedia’s article on Wayne Dyer ↗ establishes the author: an American self-help writer and motivational speaker who took an Ed.D. in guidance and counselling at Wayne State University in 1970, worked as a school guidance counsellor and ran a private therapy practice before Your Erroneous Zones (1976) made him a bestseller. Pulling Your Own Strings was the book that followed.

author.bio: Wayne Walter Dyer was an American self-help author and motivational speaker. He earned a bachelor’s degree in history and philosophy, a master’s in psychology and an Ed.D. in guidance and counselling at Wayne State University in 1970, then worked as a high-school guidance counsellor and ran a private therapy practice before Your Erroneous Zones (1976) turned him into one of the most widely read self-help writers in America. He published more than twenty books over the next four decades, Pulling Your Own Strings among the earliest.

context.heading: Why it mattered
lead: Pulling Your Own Strings followed Your Erroneous Zones ↗, the 1976 book that made Dyer one of the most-read self-help authors in America. He came to it from practice rather than theory: an Ed.D. in guidance and counselling, years as a high-school guidance counsellor and a private therapy practice. We have not read this book, so we will not summarise its argument — what the sentence itself claims is narrow enough: that where everyone is a separate case, ranking them answers nothing.

The sentence also shows why self-help quotations are so hard to source. They are written to be lifted, they circulate without their paragraph, and the books they come from are recent enough to be in copyright and old enough to be off the open web — which is exactly the gap this page is honest about.
